title: Decellularization of Porcine Right Ventricular Outflow Tracts Using 3D Printed Flow Chamber
author: Harris, Schot, et al.

steps.title: Print flow‑rig components
steps.instruction: Using a Form 3 (or equivalent) printer, print the chamber, lid and gasket with the following parameters: chamber – BioMed Clear Resin RS‑F2‑BMCL‑01, 16 h 15 min print time, support touchpoint size 0.5 mm, density 1.0 kg/m³; lid – BioMed Clear Resin RS‑F2‑BMCL‑01, 9 h 45 min print time, support touchpoint size 0.5 mm, density 1.0 kg/m³; gasket – Elastic 50A Resin RS‑F2‑ELCL‑01, 17 h 15 min print time, support touchpoint size 0.6 mm, density 0.65 kg/m³. Total printing time is 43 h 15 min.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the resins are USP Class VI certified and sourced from an FDA‑registered, EU MDR and ISO 13485 certified facility.
If using alternative printers (Form 2, 3+, 3B, 3B+, 3L, 3BL) verify that the same resins are compatible.

steps.title: Clean printed parts
steps.instruction: Flush all inlets and outlets of each printed part with a 50 mL syringe filled with propan‑2‑ol, then remove supports with clippers and tweezers being careful not to damage the parts.

substeps.instruction: Submerge each part in the Form Wash bath and agitate for 20 min in propan‑2‑ol.
Rinse each part thoroughly with fresh propan‑2‑ol.

steps.title: Cure and sterilise parts
steps.instruction: Cure the chamber and lid at 60 °C for 60 min each and the gasket at 60 °C for 20 min. After curing, autoclave the chamber, lid and gasket at 121 °C for 15 min (pre‑vacuum steam sterilisation, 4 min steam phase, 30 min dry phase, 30 min between cycles).

steps.title: Collect and transport heart
steps.instruction: Place the explanted porcine heart in a heavy‑duty polyethylene bag, keep it on ice and transport to the laboratory as quickly as possible.

steps.title: Dissect right ventricular outflow tract
steps.instruction: On a clean (non‑sterile) surface, dissect the RVOT following the sequence shown in Figure 2: identify pulmonary artery (yellow) and aorta (black), separate them with blunt‑end scissors, cut adventitia layer‑by‑layer against the aorta, insert blunt‑end tweezers into the pulmonary artery through the valve, cut the right ventricle against the tweezers with a scalpel, and finally isolate the pulmonary artery, pulmonary valve and right ventricle as a single RVOT specimen.

substeps.instruction: Discard any RVOT with holes in the pulmonary artery or visible infection (pus).
Use autoclaved (121 °C, 15 min) glassware, forceps and scissors; autoclave PBS before use.

steps.title: Initial PBS wash
steps.instruction: Place the dissected RVOT in a sterile container, submerge it in sterile PBS containing 1× penicillin/streptomycin (P/S), and sterilise the outside of the container with 70 % (v/v) ethanol before moving it into a class II biosafety cabinet.

steps.title: Wash RVOT in PBS
steps.instruction: Transfer the RVOT to a new sterile container, completely submerge it in excess autoclaved PBS with 1× P/S and agitate gently for 15 min (manual swirl or rocker). Discard the wash, remove clots with blunt‑end forceps, and repeat until the PBS runs clear (minimum three washes).

substeps.instruction: Maintain full submersion at all times.
If using a rocker, seal the container, spray the exterior with 70 % ethanol, and return it to the cabinet.

steps.title: Freeze RVOT for storage
steps.instruction: Place the washed RVOT in a TissueVault Cryogenic Freezing Bag of appropriate size, submerge the bag in Hanks’ Balanced Salt Solution (HBSS), heat‑seal the bag, place it inside a polyethylene self‑seal bag and store at –80 °C. RVOTs may be stored up to one year before decellularisation.

steps.title: Prepare Day 1 EDTA solution
steps.instruction: In a sterile 250 mL beaker prepare 0.1 % (v/v) EDTA solution in 10 mM Tris with 1× P/S: add 250 µL 0.5 M EDTA, 5 tablets Pierce A32965 protease inhibitor, 2.5 mL 100× P/S stock, and bring the volume to 250 mL with 10 mM Tris. Filter‑sterilise through a 0.2 µm membrane.

steps.title: Day 1 decellularisation
steps.instruction: Empty the flow‑chamber reservoir and sample chamber via the primary and secondary taps using a 50 mL syringe, fill the chamber with the Day 1 EDTA solution, and circulate for 24 h at 42 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Day 2 SDS solution
steps.instruction: In a sterile 250 mL beaker make 0.1 % (w/v) SDS in 10 mM Tris with 1× P/S: add 2.5 mL 10 % (w/v) SDS stock, 2.5 mL 100× P/S stock, and bring to 250 mL with 10 mM Tris. Filter‑sterilise (0.2 µm).

steps.title: Day 2 decellularisation
steps.instruction: Remove the Day 1 solution from the chamber, fill with the Day 2 SDS solution and circulate for 24 h at 42 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Day 3 PBS solution
steps.instruction: In a sterile 1 L beaker add 7.5 mL 100× P/S stock to 1 L, then make up to 750 mL with 1× PBS (final 1× PBS with 1× P/S). Use 250 mL per chamber fill.

steps.title: Day 3 solution changes
steps.instruction: Perform three PBS washes: fill chamber with 250 mL PBS‑P/S, circulate for 15 min at 42 °C, remove solution; repeat a second 15‑min circulation; fill again and circulate overnight (16–20 h) at 42 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Day 4 Benzonase solution
steps.instruction: In a sterile 250 mL beaker make 10 U/mL Benzonase in 50 mM Tris, 1 mM MgCl₂, 1× P/S: add 94 µL Benzonase stock (26.6 U/µL), 2.5 mL 100× P/S stock, and bring to 250 mL with 50 mM Tris + 1 mM MgCl₂. Filter‑sterilise (0.2 µm).

steps.title: Day 4 Benzonase treatment
steps.instruction: Replace chamber solution with the Benzonase solution, circulate for 3 h at 37 °C, then repeat the same 3 h circulation once more (two total cycles).

steps.title: Day 4 PBS washes
steps.instruction: After Benzonase cycles, replace solution with the Day 3 PBS‑P/S solution: circulate 15 min at 42 °C, remove, circulate another 15 min at 42 °C, remove, then fill and circulate for ~63–66 h at 42 °C.

steps.title: Day 5‑6 extended PBS wash
steps.instruction: Continue circulating 1× PBS with 1× P/S at 42 °C for two full days without any solution changes.

steps.title: Prepare Day 7 high‑salt solution
steps.instruction: Make two solutions: (a) 1× PBS with 1× P/S (as in Day 3) and (b) 50 mM Tris, 1.5 M NaCl, 1× P/S (add 2.5 mL 100× P/S stock to a sterile 250 mL beaker and bring to 250 mL with 50 mM Tris + 1.5 M NaCl).

steps.title: Day 7 solution changes
steps.instruction: Fill chamber with PBS‑P/S, circulate 15 min at 42 °C, then replace with the high‑salt Tris‑NaCl‑P/S solution and circulate for 24 h at 42 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Day 8 final PBS
steps.instruction: Prepare 1× PBS with 1× P/S as in Day 3 (250 mL per fill).

steps.title: Day 8 final washes
steps.instruction: Perform three PBS washes: 15 min circulation at 42 °C, remove; repeat a second 15‑min circulation, remove; fill and circulate overnight (16–20 h) at 42 °C.

steps.title: Disassemble and clean apparatus
steps.instruction: After the final wash, remove the PBS solution, disconnect all tubing, spray external surfaces with 70 % (v/v) ethanol and move the chamber back into the class II cabinet. Remove clamps, lid and gasket, cut sutures to release the decellularised RVOT (dRVOT), place the dRVOT in autoclaved PBS with 1× P/S, disassemble all tubes, connectors and hose barbs into a labelled container, and discard the taps.

substeps.instruction: The dRVOT is now ready for downstream characterisation.
Sterilise the apparatus again as described in Step 3 if it will be reused.

steps.title: Select ROIs for nuclei counting
steps.instruction: Load a down‑sampled copy of the DAPI image in ImageJ, manually draw five representative regions of interest (ROIs) and save them as ImageJ ROI files.

steps.title: Count nuclei in ROIs
steps.instruction: For each ROI, load the high‑resolution DAPI image, divide by a Gaussian‑filtered copy (sigma = 65 µm) for background correction, apply a rolling‑ball background subtraction (radius = 30 px), binarise with a user‑defined intensity threshold, delete holes <0.5 µm², median‑filter (radius = 0.3 µm), perform intensity‑based watershed to split merged nuclei, detect nuclei via connected‑components labeling, remove objects below a user‑defined area threshold, and record the nuclei count.

substeps.instruction: Average the counts from the five ROIs to obtain nuclei/µm² for the sample.
For decellularised right‑ventricle samples, perform three independent manual counts per ROI and average them before the ROI averaging.

steps.title: Process DNA quantification data
steps.instruction: In Excel, calculate the mean and standard deviation (SD) of the eight blank wells; ensure SD < 10 % of the mean. Plot the blank‑corrected standard curve (absorbance – mean blank) and compute R²; the curve must have R² ≥ 0.98 or the assay must be repeated. Use the linear equation to convert each sample’s corrected absorbance to DNA concentration, correct for any dilution factor, and normalise to dry tissue weight to obtain ng DNA per mg tissue.

substeps.instruction: If R² < 0.98, repeat the single‑strand elimination (step 72) and double‑strand quantification (step 73) before re‑calculating.
